basis: Deterministic gates re-run by the Governor rather than trusted from the builder claim.
Audit bound to the exact candidate digest; candidate mutation invalidates it.
Evidence reloaded from disk and re-verified after being written.

rounds.reviewer: independent (automated PR review + independent security review)

findings.finding: paths_in_scope used bare fnmatch, so 'src/../AGENTS.md' matched 'src/**'. A reversible write to a protected surface cleared the Governor guardrail without a human.
findings.resolution: Path scope promoted to src/forge/paths.py with normalization, traversal rejection, and segment-aware matching. execution_loop now delegates to the same implementation instead of holding a second copy.
findings.note: Found independently by two reviewers. The duplicate implementation was the root cause: one correct, one not, and the weaker one decided wherever it sat.

findings.finding: An empty touched_paths read as in-scope, because all() over an empty sequence is vacuously true. touched_paths was optional, so the callers least able to enumerate paths — shell above all — silently lost the deterministic half of the guardrail.
findings.resolution: Empty paths now fail closed; touched_paths is required.
findings.note: A test in round 1 pinned the fail-open behaviour as intended, so the suite would never have caught it.

findings.finding: CHANGED_PATHS was a hand-maintained tuple covering 13 of 33 changed paths, omitting AGENTS.md, DECISIONS.md, and the core modules. Omitted paths skipped the loop's scope validation and were absent from the exact-candidate tree hash.
findings.resolution: Changed paths derived from git, unioning committed and working-tree changes, excluding only the evidence the slice writes itself.
findings.note: This is the audit's own governance-drift finding reproduced inside the fix for it.

findings.finding: Recorded candidate identity folded in the base SHA, absolute checkout path, and branch, so --check could never pass once committed or checked out elsewhere.
findings.resolution: --check compares the content tree hash, which is what the audit binds to. Verified across a commit.

findings.finding: write() atomically replaced an existing stream's whole chain, so re-running a producer destroyed prior evidence — in a store introduced as append-only.
findings.resolution: write() requires the persisted chain to be an exact prefix and appends only new records; divergence is refused. Deliberate replacement moved to rebind(), which callers must choose.

findings.finding: The consistency gate read only README.md, leaving .agent/CURRENT_STATE.md — authority layer 6, and the other document that drifted — free to go stale while the gate stayed green.
findings.resolution: Gate scans every state-bearing document. It immediately caught two stale node statuses in CURRENT_STATE.md.

residual_risk: The slice proves the loop's control flow, not agent output quality. The first real measurement of that is still ahead, and no completed node claims otherwise.
Provider adapters are verified against injected transports and published API shapes, not against live endpoints. A wire-format change at a vendor would not be caught by CI.
Absorbing three proposed nodes into one packet is wider than the default bounded packet. It was accepted because the three were not independent.
CI has never successfully executed in this repository: the runner does not schedule the job. All gate evidence is from local runs via scripts/validate.sh.
discovery_candidates: OBS-FIX-000-unexecuted-paths-hide-defects: a defect on a code path no test or run exercises is invisible to review, however thorough.
OBS-FIX-000-duplicate-security-logic: where one security rule has two implementations, the weaker one decides wherever it sits. Both round-2 HIGH findings were duplication, not absence.
OBS-FIX-000-hand-maintained-state-recurs: the fix for hand-maintained drift introduced a hand-maintained list. Deriving state from a source of truth has to be the default, not the remedy.
